accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the principal objective of genetic medicines?
o: To prevent the formation of mitochondrial DNA
To correct or compensate for faulty genes
To replace all normal cells with genetically modified cells
accepted.x: Genetic medicines are intended to correct or compensate for faulty genes. They do not aim to replace all normal cells or prevent mitochondrial DNA formation.
accepted.tq: Use the precise functional definition rather than choosing an extreme purpose.
accepted.sec: Genetic medicine - gene therapy, MRT, recombinant vaccines  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following can serve as carriers for delivering genetic medicines?
accepted.x: Engineered viruses and lipid nanoparticles are used as carriers for delivering genetic material in genetic medicine.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the correct delivery carriers from closely related biological alternatives.
accepted.sec: Genetic medicine - gene therapy, MRT, recombinant vaccines  [other exams]

accepted.s: Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy is popularly associated with which expression?
accepted.x: Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy is popularly called the “three-parent baby” technique because mitochondrial material is obtained from a donor in addition to the nuclear genetic material of the parents.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related reproductive-technology labels.
accepted.sec: Genetic medicine - gene therapy, MRT, recombinant vaccines  [other exams]

accepted.s: Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy raises ethical concerns particularly in relation to:
accepted.x: Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy raises ethical concerns because it involves germline changes and is linked to debates over designer babies.
accepted.tq: Match the technology with the ethical issue most directly associated with it.
accepted.sec: Genetic medicine - gene therapy, MRT, recombinant vaccines  [other exams]

accepted.s: The CDSCO gene therapy rules referred to in the context of genetic medicine were issued in:

accepted.tq: Test the exact year using nearby-year distractors.
accepted.sec: Genetic medicine - gene therapy, MRT, recombinant vaccines  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding genome-edited crop varieties released or developed in India.

List-I (Variety)
a. Pusa Rice DST1
b. Kamala (DRR Dhan 100)
c. CRISPR phosphate-uptake rice

List-II (Developer)
i. NIPGR
ii. ICAR-IARI, Delhi
iii. ICAR (IIRR, Hyderabad)

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Pusa Rice DST1 was developed by ICAR-IARI, Delhi; Kamala by ICAR through IIRR, Hyderabad; and the CRISPR phosphate-uptake rice by NIPGR.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure developer-variety pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong pair.
accepted.sec: Genome-edited crop varieties released in India → developer

accepted.s: Pusa Rice DST1 is associated with which of the following traits and editing features?
o: Insect resistance; insertion of a Bt toxin gene by SDN-2
Drought and salinity tolerance; DST gene knockout by SDN-1
Higher phosphate uptake; insertion of a foreign bacterial gene
Vitamin A enrichment; mitochondrial gene replacement
accepted.x: Pusa Rice DST1 is an edited form of MTU1010, designed for drought and salinity tolerance through DST gene knockout using SDN-1.
accepted.tq: Combine the crop, trait and technical method instead of relying on the variety name alone.
accepted.sec: Genome-edited crop varieties released in India → developer

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding genome-edited crop varieties in India:
1. Kamala is also known as DRR Dhan 100.
2. Kamala is SDN-1 edited and is associated with higher yield and early maturity.
3. CRISPR phosphate-uptake rice was developed by NIPGR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Kamala is DRR Dhan 100, has the stated SDN-1 and agronomic features, and NIPGR developed the phosphate-uptake rice.
accepted.tq: When each statement matches a separate row of the crop-development data, test the combined option carefully.
accepted.sec: Genome-edited crop varieties released in India → developer

accepted.s: Pusa Rice DST1 was set for commercial launch as India’s first genome-edited rice and was to be regulated like:
accepted.x: Pusa Rice DST1 was described as India’s first genome-edited rice for commercial launch and was to be regulated like a conventional crop.
accepted.tq: Test the regulatory classification rather than the biological trait.
accepted.sec: Genome-edited crop varieties released in India → developer

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes biofortification from genetic modification?
o: GM technology uses only conventional crossing, whereas biofortification uses viral vectors.
Biofortification usually raises nutrient levels through conventional breeding, whereas GM technology inserts foreign genes.
Biofortification always requires foreign genes, whereas GM technology never changes genes.
Both terms exclusively refer to pesticide resistance.
accepted.x: Biofortification generally increases nutritional value through conventional breeding, while GM crops involve insertion of foreign genes.
accepted.tq: Separate two look-alike concepts by their defining technological method.
accepted.sec: Biofortified vs GM crops

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Pusa Rice DST1 — conventional biofortified millet
accepted.x: Dhanshakti is an iron-rich pearl millet variety associated with ICRISAT. High-lysine maize is another biofortification example, but the other matches are incorrect.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched pair among crop, trait and technology combinations.
accepted.sec: Biofortified vs GM crops

accepted.s: In the year referred to in the crop-variety data, ICAR released how many varieties, including 34 biofortified and 79 stress-tolerant varieties?
accepted.x: ICAR released 524 varieties in the stated year, of which 34 were biofortified and 79 were stress-tolerant.
accepted.tq: Use the exact total and distinguish it from nearby round-number alternatives.
accepted.sec: Biofortified vs GM crops

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety:
1. It is linked to the Convention on Biological Diversity.
2. It was adopted in 2000.
3. It entered into force in 2003.
4. India is a Party to it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Cartagena Protocol is under the CBD framework, was adopted in 2000, entered into force in 2003, and India is a Party to it.
accepted.tq: Check each treaty attribute separately before selecting the cumulative code.
accepted.sec: Global GM status and Cartagena link

accepted.s: The primary environmental concern associated with gene flow from GM crops is that transgenes may move through:
o: Cross-pollination into non-GM crops and wild relatives
accepted.x: Gene flow occurs when transgenes move through pollen and cross-pollination into non-GM crops or related wild plants.
accepted.tq: Apply the mechanism of gene flow to a field-level situation.
accepted.sec: Gene flow - transgene escape, superweeds, centres of origin  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Transfer of herbicide-tolerance from a GM crop into weedy relatives may result in:
o: Reduction in the number of plant genes
Immediate conversion of weeds into crops
Permanent loss of all soil microbes
accepted.x: Movement of herbicide-tolerance genes into weedy relatives can create invasive superweeds and increase weediness.
accepted.tq: Link the transferred trait with its most direct ecological consequence.
accepted.sec: Gene flow - transgene escape, superweeds, centres of origin  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The risk of transgene escape is considered highest in a crop’s:
accepted.x: The risk is highest in centres of origin or diversity because numerous wild relatives of the crop occur there.
accepted.tq: Use the ecological-location clue to identify where gene flow has the greatest significance.
accepted.sec: Gene flow - transgene escape, superweeds, centres of origin  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: India’s status as a centre of diversity of which crop was an important argument against Bt brinjal?
accepted.x: India is a centre of diversity of brinjal, and the presence of wild relatives was an important argument in the concern over Bt brinjal.
accepted.tq: Test the crop-specific association rather than the general concept of crop diversity.
accepted.sec: Gene flow - transgene escape, superweeds, centres of origin  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best explains genetic homogenisation in agriculture?
o: Cultivation of many locally adapted landraces in small farms
Increase in the number of unrelated crop species in a field
Exchange of seeds among farmers without commercial restrictions
Use of uniform engineered varieties over large areas, reducing agro-biodiversity
accepted.x: Genetic homogenisation results when uniform varieties are widely cultivated, reducing agro-biodiversity and increasing vulnerability to new pathogens and climate shocks.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that contains both the process and its defining consequence.
accepted.sec: Loss of crop genetic diversity - monoculture, landraces  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Monoculture and the dominance of a few patented seed firms can lead to the displacement of:
accepted.x: Monoculture and concentration of seed production can displace traditional landraces and farmer varieties.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific agricultural genetic resources affected by monoculture.
accepted.sec: Loss of crop genetic diversity - monoculture, landraces  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which technological development has been specifically flagged for its impact on biodiversity?
accepted.x: Genetic modification has been identified as the technology among these options that was flagged for its potential impact on biodiversity.
accepted.tq: Use the exclusion pattern to distinguish the biodiversity concern from unrelated technologies.
accepted.sec: Loss of crop genetic diversity - monoculture, landraces  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a safeguard for crop genetic diversity?
o: National Gene Fund — prohibition of benefit sharing
PPV&FR Act — compulsory destruction of landraces
National Genebank — promotion of genetic homogenisation
accepted.x: The National Genebank conserves accessions. The PPV&FR Act protects farmers’ varieties, landraces and wild relatives, while the National Gene Fund relates to benefit sharing.
accepted.tq: Match each safeguard with its actual conservation or benefit-sharing function.
accepted.sec: Loss of crop genetic diversity - monoculture, landraces  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The National Genebank was reported to contain approximately how many accessions?
accepted.x: The National Genebank was reported to contain 4,70,513 accessions.
accepted.tq: Read the Indian numeral grouping accurately and reject misplaced-zero alternatives.
accepted.sec: Loss of crop genetic diversity - monoculture, landraces  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes V-GURT from T-GURT?
o: V-GURT switches traits chemically, whereas T-GURT produces sterile seeds in every case.
V-GURT produces sterile seeds, whereas T-GURT switches a desired trait on or off through a proprietary chemical.
Both technologies are fully commercialised in India.
Both technologies refer only to antibiotic-resistance markers.
accepted.x: V-GURT, or terminator technology, makes the next generation of seeds non-viable. T-GURT controls expression of a desired trait using a proprietary chemical.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similar abbreviations by their mechanisms.
accepted.sec: Genetic use restriction (terminator) technology  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the status of V-GURT in India and globally?
o: It is commercialised everywhere and compulsory in India.
It is not commercialised anywhere and is banned in India under the PPV&FR Act, 2001.
It is used only in public seed banks and encouraged under the PPV&FR Act.
It is research-stage technology with no legal status in India.
accepted.x: V-GURT has not been commercialised anywhere and is banned in India under the PPV&FR Act, 2001.
accepted.tq: Combine the technology’s global status with the specific Indian legal position.
accepted.sec: Genetic use restriction (terminator) technology  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The principal concern of farmers regarding terminator technology is that it:
o: Allows farmers to reuse seed indefinitely without purchase
Increases the nutritional value of every seed
Makes all crops resistant to every insect
Prevents plants from forming viable seeds, ending normal seed saving and replanting
accepted.x: Terminator technology makes the next generation of seeds non-viable, preventing seed saving and replanting and potentially forcing annual purchases.
accepted.tq: Apply the mechanism to the farmer’s seed-saving decision.
accepted.sec: Genetic use restriction (terminator) technology  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Horizontal gene transfer in the biosafety context refers to:
o: Replacement of nuclear DNA by mitochondrial DNA in every cell
Movement of genes between unrelated organisms
Transmission of genes only from parent to offspring
Movement of pollen only within one flower
accepted.x: Horizontal gene transfer is the movement of genes between unrelated organisms. Antibiotic-resistance genes may potentially pass from environmental bacteria to human pathogens.
accepted.tq: Distinguish horizontal transfer from ordinary vertical inheritance.
accepted.sec: Biosafety concerns - allergenicity, HGT, marker genes, Mon 863  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The use of antibiotic-resistance marker genes in the construction of GM organisms raises concern primarily because such genes may:
accepted.x: Antibiotic-resistance marker genes may contribute to the spread of antibiotic resistance, which is a recognised biosafety concern.
accepted.tq: Link the marker gene with the specific public-health risk it may create.
accepted.sec: Biosafety concerns - allergenicity, HGT, marker genes, Mon 863  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Mon 863, which was in the news over the safety of feeding studies, was a genetically modified:
o: Vitamin-A enriched rice targeting night blindness
accepted.x: Mon 863 was a Monsanto genetically modified pest-resistant maize variety directed against corn rootworm and was discussed in connection with feeding-study safety.
accepted.tq: Use the crop-pest association to identify the correct GM variety.
accepted.sec: Biosafety concerns - allergenicity, HGT, marker genes, Mon 863  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a problem reported in the experience of Bt cotton cultivation?
o: Complete elimination of all sucking pests
Pink bollworm resistance to Bt toxins
accepted.x: Pink bollworm developed resistance to Bt toxins. Non-adoption of refuges and recommended practices also contributed to the problem.
accepted.tq: Identify the adverse outcome that directly reflects pest evolution.
accepted.sec: Bt cotton experience - resistance, secondary pests, outcomes  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The rise of whitefly and mealybug in Bt cotton fields illustrates the problem of:
accepted.x: Whitefly and mealybug are examples of sucking or secondary pests that increased as a problem in Bt cotton cultivation.
accepted.tq: Classify the named pests under the correct agricultural category.
accepted.sec: Bt cotton experience - resistance, secondary pests, outcomes  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which combination represents factors that contributed to difficulties associated with Bt cotton?
o: Pest resistance, non-adoption of refuges, high input costs and seed dependency
Absence of any pest resistance, free seed availability and zero input costs
Only improved soil fertility and increased landrace diversity
Exclusive control of fungal diseases through biofortification
accepted.x: The reported difficulties included pest resistance, failure to adopt refuges or recommended practices, high input costs and dependence on purchased seed.
accepted.tq: Select the option that combines the separate economic, ecological and management concerns.
accepted.sec: Bt cotton experience - resistance, secondary pests, outcomes  [GROUP-II]
